entries.effect: In bind mode (first argument not equal to unbind), bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh checks that this vendor and device ID is present at each card address before it binds the card to the vfio-pci driver (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:121-127).
entries.name: pci_id
entries.notes: The name is lower case. No comment or document in the checkout describes this read. The card list itself comes from the fixed filter lspci -d 8200: (bin/bind-cards.sh:7), so the variable does not select cards. Text that matches none of the three patterns of bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh makes that script exit with code 1 (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:83-85), and bin/bind-cards.sh then stops (set -e). Text of the form dddd:bb:dd.f or bb:dd.f replaces the card address (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:78-82). bin/reload_cards.sh:5 and bin/reset-cards:2 assign pci_id themselves, so they do not read the environment. Text with only a vendor ID, such as 8200:, also matches none of the patterns (checked on a stand-alone copy of the three regular expressions). bin/README.md:85 describes the script and does not name the variable.

readers.mechanism: shell $NAME; the script never assigns the name

entries.default: Unset or empty: the value counts as 0 (checked with bash 5.1.16), so the first address is the base address 0x37000000000.
entries.effect: On the first pass of the loop, the inherited value is added to the base address 0x37000000000. The result is the address that ./iotools mmio_write64 writes and ./iotools mmio_read64 reads. On each later pass the address of the previous pass is added to the base address again.
entries.name: start_address
entries.notes: The script reads a range column from address_map_1.csv (bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_1.sh:13) but never uses it. The sibling script assigns start_address from that column first (bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_2.sh:21) and does not read the environment. No comment or document in the checkout describes this read. The script writes to device memory, so an exported start_address changes which addresses are written.

readers.mechanism: shell $NAME read before the first assignment; the first loop pass takes the inherited value

entries.values: Hexadecimal digits without the 0x prefix. The script puts 0x in front and uses the text in bash arithmetic.
